chapters.title: Chapter 6Are Agents Really Different from Chatbots and Co-pilots?

headings.title: Chapter 6Are Agents Really Different from Chatbots and Co-pilots?

figures.caption: Figure 6.1 Bots versus autonomous agents Source: Salesforce
figures.alt: A screenshot compares Bots and Autonomous Agents in customer service scenarios. Bots provide repetitive, scripted responses and struggle to handle complex interactions effectively, often requiring repeated input from the customer. In contrast, Autonomous Agents offer dynamic and conversational interactions, combining information with action. They quickly identify issues, confirm details, and proactively provide solutions, ensuring a smoother and more customer-friendly experience.

figures.caption: Figure 7.1 Agentforce agentic loop
figures.alt: A diagram illustrates the Agentforce agentic loop within the Salesforce Platform. Data from the Data Cloud is retrieved and fed into the Agentic Loop, where it undergoes a cycle of planning, evaluation, and refinement. Based on this process, actions are taken across Customer 360 apps and channels.

chapters.title: Chapter 8What Is the Einstein Trust Layer, and Why Do You Need It?

headings.title: Chapter 8What Is the Einstein Trust Layer, and Why Do You Need It?

figures.caption: Figure 8.1 Einstein Trust Layer
figures.alt: A diagram depicts the Einstein Trust Layer, which acts as a secure intermediary between CRM Apps and various AI Models. When a prompt originates from CRM Apps, it undergoes Secure Data Retrieval, Dynamic Grounding, Data Masking, and Prompt Defense within the Trust Layer before reaching the Models. The response from the models then passes through Zero Retention, Data Demasking, Toxicity Detection, and a Feedback Framework, with an Audit Trail recording the process.

chapters.title: Chapter 9Why Do You Need Data Cloud for Agentforce?

headings.title: Chapter 9Why Do You Need Data Cloud for Agentforce?

figures.caption: Figure 9.1 How Data Cloud works
figures.alt: A diagram begins by connecting various data sources, such as Salesforce, external apps, data lakes, unstructured data, and APIs, without data duplication. These diverse data profiles are then harmonized through preparation, transformation, mapping to a unified model, and identity resolution. The harmonized data is governed by AI by tagging, classifying, defining, and enforcing policies. Finally, the data is activated anywhere, providing real-time data, insights, actions, and search capabilities, including RAG.
